rounds.text: RBZ Jewellers Ltd trades at a compelling valuation of 12.5x P/E [E1], representing a stark discount to the sector benchmark of 23.9x [E6]. This valuation disconnect is completely detached from the company's stellar fundamental performance, highlighted by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 42% [E17] and trailing twelve-month profit growth accelerating to 54% [E19]. Operational efficiency is exceptional, delivering a return on capital employed (ROCE) of 18.74% against a sector benchmark of 10.39% [E10] and a return on equity (ROE) of 18.28% compared to the sector's 9.04% [E9]. Growth momentum remains robust, evidenced by Q1 FY27 revenue surging 60% year-on-year to INR 121 crores, propelled by a 70% jump in retail revenue and a 47% increase in wholesale revenue [E70]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that the current market price only prices in a negligible 1.6% earnings growth rate [E40], providing massive upside optionality as management executes its store expansion plans and targets a balanced 50-50 B2B and B2C revenue mix [E67]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -7 crores for March 2026 [E29] alongside a temporary -2 percentage point dip in quarterly operating margins [E25].

RBZ Jewellers faces significant liquidity and structural risks, as evidenced by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -7 Cr and a negative free cash flow of Rs -40 Cr for March 2026 [E29, E30]. This poor cash conversion of -0.13x explains why the company pays no dividends despite reporting profits [E28, E54]. To fund its operations, the company is aggressively increasing its leverage, with borrowings nearly doubling to Rs 170 Cr in one year and management targeting a future debt-to-equity ratio as high as 2:1 [E32, E82]. Institutional investors have largely abandoned the stock, with foreign institutional holdings dropping from 4.33% to 0.29% and domestic institutional holdings falling from 3.03% to just 0.03% [E35, E36]. Furthermore, the business is highly volatile with a 61.8% annualized volatility and a historical drawdown of -57.4%, while earnings growth is decelerating and unhedged gold inventory exposes the firm to commodity risk [E47, E46, E60, E85]. Conceded: the company has maintained a strong five-year compounded sales growth of 43% and trades at a P/E of 12.5, which is significantly lower than the sector benchmark [E14, E1, E6].

While the bear highlights negative cash flows [E29, E30], these are the result of a deliberate capex build-up phase, evidenced by a 733.3% increase in CWIP [E33] and significant inventory deployment for new stores that are expected to break even in a year or less [E72, E66]. Although borrowings have increased [E32], the current debt-to-equity ratio remains moderate at 0.57x [E31], and the projected increase in leverage will be driven by Gold Metal Loans intended to fully hedge inventory and mitigate commodity risks [E82, E83, E85]. The claim of decelerating earnings [E60] is contradicted by a TTM profit growth of 54% [E19], which exceeds the 5-year average of 42% [E17], and a recent 60% YoY surge in Q1 revenue [E69]. Conceded: foreign and domestic institutional holdings have declined significantly [E35, E36]. However, recent institutional money flow has turned positive [E37], and the 75% promoter holding remains steadfast [E34], supporting a rules-based buy score of 92 out of 100 [E55]. Finally, the bear's focus on volatility [E47] ignores a massive 69.6% margin of safety [E39], with a DCF-derived intrinsic value of Rs 591 against a market price of only Rs 180 [E38].

While the bull frames negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -7 Cr and Rs -40 Cr as a deliberate capex build-up phase [E28, E29, E30, E33], cash generation remains severely compromised regardless of intent. Conceded: CWIP increased by 733.3% [E33] and new store break-evens are targeted within a year [E66], yet borrowings have nearly doubled to Rs 170 Cr [E32], and the company is not paying out any dividend [E54]. The bull dismisses decelerating earnings warnings [E60] by pointing to TTM profit growth [E19], but quarterly data shows operating margins contracting by 2 percentage points YoY in June 2026 [E25] alongside an inconsistent margin trend [E26, E27]. Although the bull highlights management's hedging intentions via Gold Metal Loans [E83], holding unhedged gold inventory in open positions currently exposes the business to severe commodity volatility risks [E85] compounded by stagnant gold rates that eliminate inventory gains [E84]. Finally, the bull's reliance on a DCF intrinsic value [E38] ignores that foreign and domestic institutional holdings have collapsed by 4.04 and 3.00 percentage points respectively [E35, E36], reflecting profound institutional abandonment that a slight recent uptick in money flow [E37] does not erase.

Conceded: operating and free cash flows were negative in March 2026 [E29, E30], and borrowings have increased to Rs 170 Cr [E32]. However, this is a strategic capex build-up phase evidenced by a 733.3% increase in CWIP [E33] and the hiring of up to 60 new employees for upcoming store launches [E77], which are expected to achieve capex break-even in a year or less [E66]. While the bear notes a quarterly margin dip [E25], TTM operating margins have expanded by 2 percentage points over three years [E24], and Q1 FY27 revenue grew 60% YoY [E69]. The concern regarding decelerating earnings [E60] is countered by a TTM profit growth of 54% [E19] and a 5-year profit CAGR of 42.1% [E53], which significantly outperforms the sector median of 18.2% [E63]. Management is actively addressing commodity volatility by transitioning to hedged positions via Gold Metal Loans [E83] and shifting toward a higher-margin 75% retail revenue mix [E67, E68]. Despite previous institutional exits [E35, E36], current money flow has turned positive [E37], and the stock holds a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E44]. Ultimately, the current price implies only 1.6% earnings growth [E40], leaving a 69.6% margin of safety compared to its intrinsic value of Rs 591 [E38, E39].

Conceded: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 60% YoY [E69] and 5-year profit CAGR is 42.1% [E53]. However, the bull's dismissal of cash burn ignores that operating cash flow was negative Rs 7 Cr and free cash flow plummeted to negative Rs 40 Cr in March 2026 [E29, E30]. While the bull points to a 733.3% rise in CWIP [E33] as mere growth spend, total borrowings simultaneously nearly doubled to Rs 170 Cr [E32], driving leverage higher while management explicitly plans to gear up debt-to-equity to 1.5 or 2:1 [E82]. The claim that commodity volatility is being actively addressed is aspirational, given that management admits transitioning inventory to hedged Gold Metal Loans will take three years [E83], leaving current open positions entirely exposed to risk [E85]. Furthermore, the bull celebrates positive institutional money flow [E37], but ignores the severe structural desertion where foreign and domestic institutional holdings collapsed from 4.33% and 3.03% down to 0.29% and 0.03% respectively [E35, E36]. Finally, the argument that operating margins expanded over the long term [E24] glosses over the immediate deterioration showing a quarterly drop of 2 percentage points [E25] and an inconsistent yearly margin trend [E26].

evidence.fact: Management targets a 50-50 revenue mix between B2B and B2C segments in a year or two, and 75-25 long term with retail contributing 75%.
evidence.quote: For revenue mix, we see that job work percentage right now in Quarter 1 stands at 54% and, the mix has to, I think the B2B to B2C mix has to be 50-50 or so in a year or two and in long term it will be 75-25, 75 being retail.

evidence.fact: The company expects 18 carat gold to comprise at least 20% of its corporate sales mix by the end of the year.
evidence.quote: So we have introduced this since December, our sales mix in corporate, before it was 100% 22 carat, I see by the end of this year, it will be at least 20% will be of 18 caratage.

evidence.fact: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 60% YoY to INR 121 crores, driven by robust consumer demand and higher jewellery sales.
evidence.quote: For the quarter under review, revenue from operations stood at INR121 crores registering a strong growth of 60% Y-o-Y with a revenue growth in line with the guidance shared in the previous quarter, driven by robust consumer demand, higher jewellery sales and strengthening brand recall.

evidence.fact: Retail revenue grew 70% YoY to INR 78 crores, while wholesale revenue grew 47% YoY to INR 42 crores in Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: In terms of segmental performance for the quarter, retail revenue stood at INR78 crores registering a robust 70% Y-o-Y growth. Wholesale revenue stood at 42% reflecting a strong 47% Y-o-Y growth.

evidence.fact: Corporate demand was good in Q1 and management anticipates a favorable response from the B2B segment ahead of Quarter 3.
evidence.quote: So, the demand, all the corporates are giving us orders because of the upcoming season that is Quarter 3 and demand in corporates for Quarter 1 has also been good. I think we are anticipating a good response from the B2B side as well.

evidence.fact: Large format stores carry a carpet area of 10,000 square feet with INR 125 crores to INR 150 crores in inventory deployment.
evidence.quote: The large format stores are typically around 10,000 square feet carpet area and mid format stores are 5,000 square feet carpet area. The inventory deployment in large format stores is typically around INR125 crores to INR150 crores.

evidence.fact: Small format stores require inventory deployment of around INR 50 crores plus or minus 10% to 15%.
evidence.quote: While in small format stores are around INR50 crores, plus and minus 10%, 15%.

evidence.fact: The capex incurred for the upcoming Surat store is approximately INR 10 crores.
evidence.quote: Approximately INR10 crores is the capex incurred for Surat store.

evidence.fact: Q1 FY27 EBITDA reached INR 18 crores with a 14.9% margin, while Profit After Tax was INR 9 crores with a 7.5% margin.
evidence.quote: EBITDA for the quarter is INR18 crores reflecting a healthy growth of 39% Y-o-Y, with EBITDA margins coming in a healthy 14.9%. Profit after tax for the quarter has been 28% at INR9 crores translating PAT at 7.5%.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margins were impacted by stagnant average gold rates, lease asset amortization of INR 76 lakhs, and lease liability impact of INR 115 lakhs.
evidence.quote: One is that the average gold rate has remained stagnant and thus there is negligible inventory gain in the system as of now. So, on the Quarter 1 side the EBITDA margins have reflected that. There is other two impacts that are there: The amortization of lease assets is INR76 lakhs and the impact of lease liabilities is at INR115 lakhs.

evidence.fact: Employee expenses were higher after hiring 52 to 60 employees for upcoming store openings.
evidence.quote: Approximately 52 to 60 people were hired.

evidence.fact: Factory capacity stands at 1.8 to 2 tons per year, with current utilization running at around 50%.
evidence.quote: The total capacity still remains at around 1.8 to 2 tons a year. And the production that we are doing or the consumption that we are able to do is somewhere around 900 kgs to 1000 kgs. So, we are utilizing factory at around 50% of capacity.

evidence.fact: During peak festive months, factory capacity utilization increases to between 70% and 90%.
evidence.quote: In the season times, currently as of now, our capacity utilization generally goes at 70%, 80% minimum, 75%, 85% sometimes, depending on which days are all, sometimes it is near to 90% or so.

evidence.fact: Strong design appreciation from corporate customers resulted in full order books for July and August.
evidence.quote: There has been a good, successful appreciation of designs even from corporate end, because of which the July, August order kitty are full.

evidence.fact: The company holds a sanctioned debt of around INR 300 crores, which is sufficient to fund four store launches in the current financial year.
evidence.quote: Given that we have a sanctioned debt of around INR300 crores. And we are yet to utilize it, which is sufficient for the four stores that is coming in this financial year.

evidence.fact: RBZ Jewellers expects its debt-to-equity ratio to remain below 1:1 by the end of the financial year before gearing up to 1.5 to 2:1 using Gold Metal Loans.
evidence.quote: By the end of this financial year, we will be still below 1:1 ratio. I guess 0.8 will be debt and 1 equity. Over the period of time we are wanting to gear up this to 1.5 or 2:1 debt equity ratio, wherein major leverage will be through Gold Metal Loan

evidence.fact: Management plans to fully churn inventory into hedged positions using Gold Metal Loans over a three-year period.
evidence.quote: GML we are planning that during the course of the journey we should actually have an inventory which is hedged. We have already started using GML in this quarter, a little bit, but as and when the quarter passes we want to completely churn over the whole inventory to go hedged. But that will take three year of time that I, as you have said.

evidence.fact: Stagnant average gold prices in Q1 resulted in negligible inventory gain across the system.
evidence.quote: One is that the average gold rate has remained stagnant and thus there is negligible inventory gain in the system as of now.

evidence.fact: Holding unhedged gold inventory in open positions exposes the business to commodity volatility risks.
evidence.quote: Now what you talk about the inventory levels, it is a directional call that we have taken that on an ongoing business if we were to, put our inventory and this amount of inventory onto, let's say in an open position, it is going to call for risk.

evidence.quote: Certainly, I think these restrictions are not advantageous, but up to what level there is an impact is crucial.
